summary: Implementation fully matches the locked plan for issue #451. pr_creator.py routes the PR-open step through the per-call injected ForgeClient (D1, no constructor injection), removes _PR_URL_PATTERN in favor of an empty-string-only guard (D7), builds RepoRef.from_url(remote_url or repo_url), and maps both GitHubClientError and lazily-imported BitBucketClientError to PullRequestError preserving operation/structured returncode (status None->0)/redacted stderr|body/head_sha (D2); git push, pre-push diagnostics, redaction, and the existing_pr_url reuse early-return are unchanged. execution_flow.py resolves the forge client via make_forge_client(concrete_forge_for_repo(profile.forge, ws.repo_url), self._runner) inside the existing try, uses async with, passes forge_client/repo_url, and removes the new_pr_unsupported_forge_error fail-fast gate (stale comment updated; unsupported_forge_error retained). Tests cover R-gh, R-err-gh, R-bb, R-err-bb (+status=None->0), R-repo (bitbucket/github/remote_url-wins), reuse-path with a raising forge client, no-URL guard, push-failure, and R-resolve (github+bitbucket). Change set is file-disjoint with sibling Cluster B (only pr_creator.py, execution_flow.py, and their two test files); the now-dead new_pr_unsupported_forge_error stays covered by the untouched test_executor_forge_gate.py per the documented decision.
